NM-2026-SJM1.title: UNIFORM REDISTRICTING CRITERIA

actions.text: Sent to Senate Rules Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee

NM-2026-SJM1.aiSummary: This memorial would urge the U.S. Congress to pass a law that sets the same redistricting rules for congressional districts across states. It would also ask Congress to ban midcycle redistricting, unless a court orders it. The memorial would affect how congressional seats are drawn, but it would not change state law by itself.

NM-2026-SB49.title: SCHOOL-AGE APPROPRIATE FILTERING PROJECT

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Education Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB49.policyArea: CULTURAL AFFAIRS (arts, museums, libraries), EDUCATION, OTHER
NM-2026-SB49.aiSummary: The bill would create a three-year pilot project in the Public Education Department for schools and charter schools to use a rating system for library materials based on age appropriateness. Selected participants would share rated book lists with parents, gather parent feedback, and give parents a survey about the system. It would give each participant two $25,000 grants and set aside $3,210,000 for the project from fiscal years 2027 through 2029.

NM-2026-SB263.title: PUBLIC PEACE, HEALTH, SAFETY & WELFARE
NM-2026-SB263.aiSummary: A bill about public peace, health, safety, and welfare was postponed indefinitely in the Senate Judiciary Committee.

NM-2026-SB254.title: TRUNKED RADIO SUBSCRIBER FEES

actions.text: DO PASS, as amended, committee report adopted
Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Health and Public Affairs Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB254.aiSummary: The bill would set aside $2.8 million from the general fund for the Department of Information Technology. The money would pay subscriber fees for the state’s digital trunked radio communications system for city, county, and tribal public safety agencies that handle police, fire, medical, or other emergency work. The funds would be available in fiscal year 2027 and later years, and unused money would stay available instead of going back to the general fund.

NM-2026-SB222.title: PHYSICIAN RESIDENCY PROGRAMS

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Health and Public Affairs Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB222.aiSummary: The bill would give $20 million from the general fund to the Health Care Authority for fiscal years 2027 through 2029. The money would be used to create new physician residency programs and residency positions, which train doctors after medical school.

NM-2026-SB204.title: FUNDING FOR TERMINATED RESEARCH PROJECTS

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Education Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB204.aiSummary: The bill would give $100 million from the state general fund to the Higher Education Department for fiscal years 2027 and 2028. The money would help cover reduced or ended federal funding for existing research projects at the University of New Mexico, New Mexico State University, and the New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology. It would apply to projects that could still be finished if the funding gap were filled.

NM-2026-SB169.title: COST-OF-LIVING FOR SOME RETIREES

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Health and Public Affairs Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB169.policyArea: OFFICERS & EMPLOYEES, PUBLIC, STATE AGENCIES & DEPARTMENTS (including reorganization)
NM-2026-SB169.aiSummary: The bill would change how some retired public employees get cost-of-living raises. It would give a 1.68% raise on July 1, 2026 to certain retired members age 65 or older, and it would keep other raise rules for some long-term retirees, disability retirees, and older retirees. It would also set aside $10 million from the general fund for the retirement agency to pay for this in fiscal years 2027 and 2028.

NM-2026-SB146.title: CIVIL RIGHTS ACT CLAIM CHANGES

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Health and Public Affairs Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee

NM-2026-SB146.policyArea: FINANCE, PUBLIC, STATE AGENCIES & DEPARTMENTS (including reorganization)
NM-2026-SB146.aiSummary: This bill would change New Mexico’s civil rights law for claims against public bodies, which include state and local government bodies and some related groups. It would set new damage limits, bar punitive damages, shorten the time to file a claim from three years to two, and require written notice within 90 days in most cases. It would also say a person cannot collect damages under both this law and the Tort Claims Act for the same event.

NM-2026-HB40.title: TEMPORARY ERB MEMBER PAYMENT

actions.text: Sent to House Education Committee & House Appropriations & Finance Committee

NM-2026-HB40.policyArea: EDUCATION, OTHER, OFFICERS & EMPLOYEES, PUBLIC, SENIOR CITIZENS
NM-2026-HB40.aiSummary: The bill would give retired members under the Educational Retirement Act a one-time extra payment each year in fiscal years 2027 and 2028. The payment would equal 2% of their annual annuity and would not be added into future payments. It would also set aside $65.5 million from the general fund to pay for these extra payments.

NM-2026-HB278.title: TOXICOLOGY REIMBURSEMENT REQUIREMENTS

actions.text: Sent to House Health & Human Services Committee & House Appropriations & Finance Committee

NM-2026-HB278.aiSummary: The bill would set Medicaid payment rules for toxicology lab tests done by independent reference labs. It would require the state health agency to set billing codes and rules for these tests, based on medical need and clinical guidance, and it would allow the agency to check that a lab meets the program rules. The bill also sets aside $100,000 for fiscal year 2027 to carry out this payment system, and it would take effect on July 1, 2026.

NM-2026-HB110.title: HOUSING DEVELOPMENT DATA REPORTING

actions.text: DO NOT PASS, replaced with committee substitute
Sent to House Rural Development, Land Grants and Cultural Affairs Committee & House Government, Elections and Indian Affairs Committee
Sent to House Government, Elections and Indian Affairs Committee & House Rural Development, Land Grants and Cultural Affairs Committee

NM-2026-HB110.policyArea: LOCAL GOVERNMENT, PROPERTY (conservancy districts, land grants, real estate)
NM-2026-HB110.aiSummary: Beginning July 1, 2026, certain New Mexico counties and cities would have to post quarterly housing development reports on their websites. The reports would cover residential land use and building permit applications, approval or denial status, processing times, staff levels, and could include short notes to explain the data. The rule would apply to class A counties and municipalities with more than 30,000 people.
